- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid overcorrecting downward; add 2–5% buffer to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model often misreads momentum — align forecast with sentiment mean over 3–5 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend instead of 30-day trend.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), reduce forecast confidence and use weighted average of 7-day and 30-day trends.
